blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 4 allows Parliament to enact laws under Articles 2 and 3 to alter boundaries, names, or admit new states.
Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 automatically amend the First Schedule (list of States/UTs) and Fourth Schedule (Rajya Sabha seat allocation).
Such laws contain supplemental, incidental, and consequential provisions regarding representation in Parliament and state legislatures.
Laws under Article 4 are passed through an ordinary legislative procedure and simple majority, without triggering Article 368.

rows: Admission, establishment, or alteration of States/UTs
Amending general or core provisions of the Constitution
Special Majority (2/3rd present & voting + majority of total membership)
Not deemed as a formal Constitutional Amendment

items: Laws passed under Article 2 and Article 3 do NOT count as Constitutional Amendments under Article 368.
State reorganization laws require only a Simple Majority in Parliament, not a Special Majority.
Article 4 specifically mandates adjustments to the First and Fourth Schedules of the Indian Constitution.
